fields.title: Synopsis
fields.description: A debut YA crime thriller as addictive as Serial and as page-turning as One of Us Is Lying The case is closed. Five years ago, schoolgirl Andie Bell was murdered by Sal Singh. The police know he did it. Everyone in town knows he did it. Almost everyone. Having grown up in the small town that was consumed by the crime, Pippa Fitz-Amobi chooses the case as the topic for her final project. But when Pip starts uncovering secrets that someone in town desperately wants to stay hidden, what starts out as a project begins to become Pip's dangerous reality ... Perfect for fans of One of Us Is Lying, Gone Girl, We Were Liars and Riverdale Holly Jackson is 25 years old. She grew up in Buckinghamshire and started writing stories from a young age, completing her first attempt at a novel aged fifteen. She is a massive true-crime fan and her hobbies include binge-playing video games and pointing out grammatical errors in street signs.

fields.title: Synopsis
fields.description: I love him so totally, completely, sometimes it threatens to overwhelm me. Sometimes I think . . . No. I won't write about that.ALICIAAlicia Berenson writes a diary as a release, an outlet - and to prove to her beloved husband that everything is fine. She can't bear the thought of worrying Gabriel, or causing him pain.Until, late one evening, Alicia shoots Gabriel five times and then never speaks another word.THEOForensic psychotherapist Theo Faber is convinced he can successfully treat Alicia, where all others have failed. Obsessed with investigating her crime, his discoveries suggest Alicia's silence goes far deeper than he first thought.And if she speaks, would he want to hear the truth?THE SILENT PATIENT is a heart-stopping debut thriller about a woman's brutal and random act of violence against her husband - and the man obsessed with discovering why.

fields.title: Synopsis
fields.description: The Kite Runner of Khaled Hosseini's deeply moving fiction debut is an illiterate Afghan boy with an uncanny instinct for predicting exactly where a downed kite will land. Growing up in the city of Kabul in the early 1970s, Hassan was narrator Amir's closest friend even though the loyal 11-year-old with "a face like a Chinese doll" was the son of Amir's father's servant and a member of Afghanistan's despised Hazara minority. But in 1975, on the day of Kabul's annual kite-fighting tournament, something unspeakable happened between the two boys

fields.name: The Birth of Islington Marketplace: By the Students, For the Students
fields.description:
In the heart of Islington, something remarkable has begun to take shape—a marketplace built not by big corporations or established retailers, but by students themselves. The Islington Marketplace is a digital-first initiative created by the students, for the students, with one clear mission: to make buying, selling, and exchanging goods easier, more affordable, and more accessible within the student community.

The idea emerged from a simple observation: students often struggle with limited budgets, unused items piling up in hostels and apartments, and the constant need for affordable study materials, electronics, and daily essentials. Instead of relying on external platforms that do not truly reflect student life, a group of determined learners from Islington decided to build their own solution. Thus, Islington Marketplace was born.

What sets this marketplace apart is its community-driven nature. Every feature, every category, and every design decision was made with the needs of students in mind. Categories include books, electronics, bags, food, and more, ensuring that the most essential items for student life are always within reach. Beyond that, the platform provides an opportunity for budding entrepreneurs among students to test their ideas and products in a safe, supportive environment.

At its core, the Islington Marketplace is more than just a buying-and-selling platform. It is a collaborative ecosystem that fosters sustainability through reusing and recycling, promotes financial independence by allowing students to earn, and builds a stronger sense of connection within the Islington community. Instead of throwing away old textbooks or gadgets, students can now pass them on to someone who truly needs them, often at a fraction of the price.

The marketplace also embodies the spirit of innovation and digital transformation. By leveraging technology to solve real problems, the students of Islington are setting an example of how youth-driven solutions can make an impact. It reflects not just commerce, but creativity, responsibility, and empowerment.

As the platform continues to grow, its vision is clear: to become a self-sustaining hub where students can support each other, find what they need, and make student life easier and more affordable. The Islington Marketplace is proof that when young people come together, they can create something powerful and lasting.

This isn’t just a marketplace. It’s a movement of students helping students—a legacy that will shape the way the Islington community thrives for years to come.
